S01-01.method: solve the two equations of motion and eliminate a
S01-01.working: 2mg - T = 2ma and T - mg = ma; adding gives mg = 3ma so a = g/3; T = m(g + a) = m(g + g/3) = 4mg/3

S01-02.method: reduce the parallel pair, then divide the supply

S01-03.method: balance weight against drag by dimensions
S01-03.working: weight ~ rho_w g r^3 and drag ~ rho_air r^2 v^2; equating them cancels r^2 and one r, leaving v^2 ~ r, so v ~ sqrt(r)

S01-04.method: momentum first, then energy in the spring

S01-05.method: differentiate P(R) and set to zero
S01-05.working: P = E^2 R/(R + r)^2; dP/dR = 0 at R = r; then P = E^2 r/(2r)^2 = E^2/(4r)

S01-06.method: turn a pressure into a mass through g
S01-06.working: p = 1.0e5 Pa is a weight per square metre, so W = 1.0e5 N on 1 m^2; m = W/g = 1.0e5/10 = 1.0e4 kg

S01-07.method: find the speed at h, then double the time to the apex
S01-07.working: v^2 = u^2 - 2gh at height h; time from h up to the apex is v/g and the return takes the same, so the interval is 2v/g = 2sqrt(u^2 - 2gh)/g

S01-08.working: weight 20 x 10 = 200 N at 2.0 m; the perpendicular component of T at 4.0 m is T sin30 = T/2; 200 x 2.0 = (T/2) x 4.0 gives 400 = 2T so T = 200 N

S01-09.method: set the contact force to zero at the top
S01-09.working: mg - N = mv^2/r and the car leaves when N = 0, so v^2 = rg = 20 x 10 = 200; v = 14.1 m/s, so it leaves above about 14 m/s

S01-10.method: recognise an odd-harmonic series and find its step
S01-10.working: a pipe closed at one end gives only odd multiples of f0; the three given frequencies differ by 200 Hz, and 100, 300, 500, 700 are the odd multiples 1, 3, 5, 7 of 100 Hz, so f0 = 100 Hz

S01-11.method: put the critical angle equal to the fixed 45 degrees
S01-11.working: TIR needs theta > theta_c with sin(theta_c) = 1/n; the geometry fixes theta = 45, so the smallest n is the equality case 1/sin45 = 1/(1/sqrt2) = sqrt2

S01-12.working: the marked point is 6.0 V and 0.40 A; R = V/I = 6.0/0.40 = 15 ohm

S01-13.method: set heat lost equal to heat gained

S01-14.method: share the energy in inverse proportion to mass
S01-14.working: equal and opposite momenta, so KE = p^2/2m means KE goes as 1/m; the alpha has mass number 4 and the recoil A - 4, so the alpha takes (A-4)/((A-4)+4) = (A-4)/A of E

S01-15.method: substitute the constant-volume area into R = rho L / A
S01-15.working: volume fixed means A -> A/(1 + x); R' = rho L(1 + x)/(A/(1 + x)) = R(1 + x)^2; the fractional change is 2x + x^2, which for small x is 2x

S01-16.working: the gradient of a v-t graph is a, and a is -g throughout, so every section must be straight with the same slope -- that rules out the curved graphs; and each bounce returns less speed, so the peaks must shrink -- that rules out the equal-peak graph; only E has both

S01-17.method: add the gravity component and limiting friction, then equate to mg
S01-17.working: down the slope: mg sin(theta) = 5.0 x 10 x 0.60 = 30 N; normal reaction 5.0 x 10 x 0.80 = 40 N so limiting friction 0.50 x 40 = 20 N; needed pull 30 + 20 = 50 N; the hanging weight is 10m, so m = 5.0 kg

S01-18.method: require the centripetal acceleration to be g, then convert to a period
S01-18.working: omega^2 r = g so omega^2 = 10/50 = 0.20 and omega = 0.447 rad/s; T = 2 pi/omega = 6.283/0.447 = 14.1 s; equivalently T = 2 pi sqrt(r/g) = 2 pi sqrt5 = 14.1 s

S01-19.method: take the area of the triangle under the straight region
S01-19.working: energy per unit volume = (1/2) x stress x strain = 0.5 x 3.0e8 x 1.5e-3 = 0.5 x 4.5e5 = 2.25e5, which is 2.3e5 J/m^3 to two figures

S01-20.method: use sin(theta) <= 1 and round the inequality down
S01-20.working: d = 1e-3/500 = 2.0e-6 m and lambda = 6.0e-7 m; d/lambda = 2.0e-6/6.0e-7 = 3.33; n <= 3.33 so the highest order is 3; the fourth would need sin(theta) = 4 x 0.30 = 1.20, which does not exist

S01-21.method: combine the critical angle with Snell's law at the end face
S01-21.working: sin(theta_c) = 1.2/1.5 = 0.8; the steepest guided ray makes 90 - theta_c with the axis, so sin(alpha) = cos(theta_c) = sqrt(1 - 0.64) = 0.6; Snell gives sin(theta_a) = 1.5 x 0.6 = 0.9, which is also sqrt(1.5^2 - 1.2^2) = sqrt0.81

S01-23.method: conserve charge over the new total capacitance
S01-23.working: Q = CV = 2.0e-6 x 100 = 2.0e-4 C; the charge is shared over 2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0 uF; V = 2.0e-4/5.0e-6 = 40 V

S01-24.method: add the water pressure to the atmosphere, then use Boyle's law
S01-24.working: p_bottom = 1.0e5 + 1000 x 10 x 20 = 1.0e5 + 2.0e5 = 3.0e5 Pa; isothermal, so p1 V1 = p2 V2 gives 3.0e5 x 1.0 = 1.0e5 x V2 and V2 = 3.0 cm^3

S01-25.method: raise one half to the power of the number of half-lives

S02-01.method: match dimensions and take the square root
S02-01.working: [v] = L T^-1; [gamma] = N/m = M T^-2; [rho] = M L^-3; [lambda] = L. Try gamma/(rho lambda): (M T^-2)/((M L^-3)(L)) = (M T^-2)/(M L^-2) = L^2 T^-2; square root gives L T^-1, which is a speed. The other four: sqrt(gamma rho/lambda) = M L^-2 T^-1; sqrt(gamma lambda/rho) = L^2 T^-1; gamma/(rho lambda) = L^2 T^-2; sqrt(gamma rho)/lambda = M L^-5/2 T^-1

S02-02.method: write the self-similar relation and solve the quadratic
S02-02.working: R_eq = R + R R_eq/(R + R_eq); multiply out: R_eq^2 = R^2 + R R_eq; R_eq^2 - R R_eq - R^2 = 0; R_eq = R(1 + sqrt5)/2. Numerical check with R = 1: 1 + 1.618/2.618 = 1 + 0.618 = 1.618, which is the root

S02-03.method: threshold wavelength gives the work function, then subtract
S02-03.working: hc = 1240 eV nm, so the threshold photon energy is 1240/620 = 2.0 eV and that is the work function. At 310 nm the photon energy is 1240/310 = 4.0 eV. Kinetic energy = 4.0 - 2.0 = 2.0 eV

S02-04.method: build the series and sum it
S02-04.working: t_0 = sqrt(2h/g). Rebound to h/4 gives a rise-and-fall of 2 sqrt(2(h/4)/g) = 2 x (1/2) sqrt(2h/g) = t_0, so the bounces are t_0, t_0/2, t_0/4, ... Total = t_0 + t_0(1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + ...) = t_0 + t_0 x 2 = 3 sqrt(2h/g)

S02-05.method: divide the two force equations to kill the tension
S02-05.working: T cos(theta) = mg and T sin(theta) = m omega^2 L sin(theta) so T = m omega^2 L; dividing gives 1/cos(theta) = omega^2 L/g, so omega^2 = g/(L cos theta) and T = 2 pi sqrt(L cos theta/g)

S02-06.working: mass arriving per second = rho A v; it carries speed v and leaves with none, so the momentum destroyed per second is (rho A v)(v) = rho A v^2, and that is the force. Units: (kg m^-3)(m^2)(m^2 s^-2) = kg m s^-2 = N

S02-07.method: write the extension for each wire and equate
S02-07.working: e = FL/(AE) for the first. For the second A falls by a factor of four (diameter halved) and L doubles, so e = F2(2L)/((A/4)E) = 8 F2 L/(AE). Equating: F L/(AE) = 8 F2 L/(AE) so F2 = F/8

S02-08.method: approaching source, so the denominator is v minus the source speed

S02-09.method: apply the minimum-deviation relation and undo the sine
S02-09.working: n sin(A/2) = sin((A + D)/2) with A = 60 and n = sqrt2: sqrt2 x sin30 = sqrt2 x 0.5 = 0.7071 = sin45, so (60 + D)/2 = 45 and D = 30 deg

S02-10.method: common voltage, so power goes as 1/R
S02-10.working: P_3 = V^2/3 and P_6 = V^2/6, total = V^2(2/6 + 1/6) = V^2/2. Fraction = (V^2/3)/(V^2/2) = 2/3, and the smaller resistor takes the larger share

S02-11.method: count the halvings on a logarithmic axis
S02-11.working: 800/100 = 8 and 8 = 2^3, so three halvings span the twelve minutes; T = 12/3 = 4 min. Check: 800 -> 400 -> 200 -> 100 lands on the stated point

S02-12.method: reduce from the inside out, keeping the internal resistance in the loop
S02-12.working: 6 || 6 = 3; R_ext = 3 + 3 = 6; R_total = 6 + 2 = 8; I = 12/8 = 1.5 A; P = I^2 R = 2.25 x 3 = 6.75 W. Check: terminal p.d. 12 - 3 = 9 V, drop across the 3 ohm is 4.5 V, leaving 4.5 V across the pair, which 1.5 A gives

S02-13.method: conserve momentum, then divide by the combined mass
S02-13.working: p_before = 2.0 x 3.0 = 6.0 kg m/s; p_after = (2.0 + 2.0)v = 4.0v; v = 6.0/4.0 = 1.5 m/s. Energy check: 9.0 J before, 4.5 J after, so half is lost, which is what sticking means

S02-14.method: conserve charge, then compare the two energies
S02-14.working: Q = CV is fixed. C_total = C + 2C = 3C so V_new = Q/(3C) = V/3. E_before = Q^2/(2C); E_after = Q^2/(6C). Ratio 1/3 remains, so 2/3 is lost. Check: the result contains no resistance, so a thicker wire loses the same 2/3

S02-15.method: floating means submerged fraction equals the density ratio
S02-15.working: rho_L V_sub g = rho_b V g so V_sub/V = rho_b/rho_L. Water: 3/4 = rho_b/1000 so rho_b = 750. Unknown liquid: 1/2 = 750/rho_L so rho_L = 1500 kg/m^3. Direction: denser liquid holds the block higher, and 1/2 < 3/4

S02-16.method: longest wavelength that still gives a minimum
S02-16.working: delta = 3.5 - 2.5 = 1.0 m. Minimum needs delta = (n + 1/2)lambda, so the longest wavelength is at n = 0: lambda = 2 x 1.0 = 2.0 m. f = 340/2.0 = 170 Hz. Next member: lambda = 1.0/1.5 = 0.67 m giving 510 Hz, so 170 Hz is the lowest

S02-17.method: gradient gives stiffness, then convert to the modulus

S02-18.method: reduce to a proportionality before putting anything in
S02-18.working: E = hc/lambda and N = P/E, so N = P lambda/(hc) and N is proportional to P lambda. Doubling P doubles N; halving lambda halves N; the product of the two factors is 2 x 1/2 = 1, so N is unchanged

S02-19.method: divide by the large quantity, then expand
S02-19.working: kK/(k + K); divide top and bottom by K: k/(1 + k/K). With x = k/K small and n = -1, (1 + x)^n = 1 + nx gives 1 - k/K, so the result is k(1 - k/K). Numerical check with k = 1, K = 100: 100/101 = 0.990099 and 1 - 0.01 = 0.99

S02-20.method: count the positions in the ring, then remove the object
S02-20.working: Repeated reflection in two planes meeting at 60 deg is rotation in steps of 60 deg, so the bead and its images occupy 360/60 = 6 equally spaced positions. One of those is the bead, so the number of images is 6 - 1 = 5

S02-21.working: Every pair of levels gives a possible photon energy, because a single gamma can carry the whole difference. With four levels: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. The six differences are 7, 6, 4, 3, 2 and 1 MeV, all distinct

S02-22.working: v_1 - v_2 = g(t + delta_t) - g t = g delta_t, a constant. Separation = (1/2)g(t + delta_t)^2 - (1/2)g t^2 = g delta_t t + (1/2)g delta_t^2, which is linear in t. So it grows at a constant rate. At t = 0 it is already (1/2)g delta_t^2, the head start

S02-23.method: pressure balance at the lower mercury surface
S02-23.working: rho_oil h = rho_Hg (2x), so x = rho_oil h/(2 rho_Hg). In centimetres: 850 x 16/(2 x 13600) = 13600/27200 = 0.5 cm = 5.0 mm. Check the size: 0.5/16 = 1/32, and the densities are in the ratio 13600/850 = 16

S02-24.method: density times volume, then check against a known mass
S02-24.working: V = 10 x 8 x 3 = 240 m^3; m = 1.2 x 240 = 288 kg, about 300 kg. Check: the same room full of water would be 240 x 1000 = 240000 kg, and air is about a thousandth as dense, so a few hundred kilograms is right

S02-25.method: find the photon energy, double it, subtract the same work function
S02-25.working: hf = phi + E_k = 2.0 + 1.0 = 3.0 eV. Halving lambda doubles hf to 6.0 eV. The work function is a property of the metal, so E_k = 6.0 - 2.0 = 4.0 eV. Check the direction: the photon energy doubled but the kinetic energy went up by four, which is what a fixed subtraction does

S03-01.method: take moments about B, so the unknown there drops out
S03-01.working: uniform beam: the 240 N acts at the 3.0 m midpoint. The load is 2.0 m from A, so 6.0 - 2.0 = 4.0 m from B. F_A x 6.0 = 240 x 3.0 + 360 x 4.0 = 720 + 1440 = 2160; F_A = 2160/6.0 = 360 N. Check: the two supports carry 600 N, so B has 240 N, and moments about A give F_B x 6.0 = 240 x 3.0 + 360 x 2.0 = 1440, F_B = 240 N

S03-02.method: put each candidate through the base dimensions
S03-02.working: [gamma] = N/m = kg s^-2; [rho] = kg m^-3; [r] = m; want s^-1. gamma/(rho r^3) = (kg s^-2)/((kg m^-3)(m^3)) = (kg s^-2)/kg = s^-2, and the square root is s^-1, a frequency. Rejected: gamma/(rho r) gives m^2 s^-2, whose root is m s^-1, a speed; gamma r^3/rho gives m^6 s^-2; gamma rho/r^3 gives kg^2 m^-6 s^-2; and gamma/(rho r^3) without the root is a frequency squared

S03-03.method: set limiting friction equal to the weight
S03-03.working: the wall pushes back horizontally with the whole push, so N = F and the limiting friction is mu N = 0.40 F. On the point of sliding down, 0.40 F = mg = 2.0 x 10 = 20 N, so F = 20/0.40 = 50 N. Check: F = 50 N gives N = 50 N and f_max = 20 N, exactly the weight, so the block is on the point of moving and no smaller push holds

S03-04.method: balance is a ratio between the two dividers
S03-04.working: balance needs the detector nodes at the same potential: 3.0/3.0 = 6.0/R, so R = 6.0 k. Check by potentials: the top node sits at 12 x 6.0/(3.0 + 6.0) = 8.0 V and the bottom node at 12 x 6.0/(3.0 + 6.0) = 8.0 V, equal, so no current flows through G

S03-05.method: turn the gradient into a rate of climb
S03-05.working: a 10% gradient means tan(theta) = 0.10, and at that small angle sin(theta) is also about 0.10. Rising at 5.0 x 0.10 = 0.50 m/s against a weight of 80 x 10 = 800 N needs 800 x 0.50 = 400 W. Check the size: lifting 800 N half a metre every second is 400 J per second

S03-06.method: split the area into two triangles and a rectangle
S03-06.working: 0-2.0 s: (1/2) x 2.0 x 12 = 12 m. 2.0-5.0 s: 3.0 x 12 = 36 m. 5.0-8.0 s: (1/2) x 3.0 x 12 = 18 m. Total 12 + 36 + 18 = 66 m. Check: holding the peak 12 m/s for the whole 8.0 s would be 96 m, and the two ramps take away 12 + 18 = 30 m, leaving 66 m

S03-07.method: use the elastic result for a stationary target
S03-07.working: v_target = 2 m u/(m + 3m) = 2mu/(4m) = u/2. Check against both conservation laws: the incoming particle keeps (m - 3m)/(4m) u = -u/2, so p_after = m(-u/2) + 3m(u/2) = mu = p_before; and KE after = (1/2)m(u/2)^2 + (1/2)(3m)(u/2)^2 = mu^2/8 + 3mu^2/8 = mu^2/2 = KE before

S03-08.method: count three loops, so the length holds three half wavelengths
S03-08.working: the third harmonic has three loops, so L = 3 lambda/2 and lambda = 2L/3 = 2(0.60)/3 = 0.40 m. f = v/lambda = 120/0.40 = 300 Hz. Check: the fundamental is v/2L = 120/1.2 = 100 Hz and the third harmonic is 3 x 100 = 300 Hz

S03-09.method: divide the real depth by the refractive index
S03-09.working: for near-normal viewing the apparent depth is real depth / n = 2.4/1.5 = 1.6 m. Check the direction: a ray leaving the water bends away from the normal, so the stone is seen higher than it is, and 1.6 is less than 2.4

S03-10.method: reduce the loaded pair, then divide the supply
S03-10.working: the load puts 3.0 k in parallel with 3.0 k: (3.0 x 3.0)/(3.0 + 3.0) = 1.5 k. Total 6.0 + 1.5 = 7.5 k, so the parallel section takes 12 x 1.5/7.5 = 2.4 V. Check against the unloaded divider: without the load the tap gives 12 x 3.0/9.0 = 4.0 V, and loading a divider can only pull the tap down, so 2.4 is less than 4.0

S03-11.working: energy = mL = 0.50 x 2.3e6 = 1.15e6 J. t = E/P = 1.15e6/2000 = 575 s. Check the size: 575 s is a little under ten minutes, which is the right order for boiling away half a kilogram of already-boiling water

S03-12.method: show that volume and mass both go as A
S03-12.working: V = (4/3) pi r^3 = (4/3) pi r0^3 A, so the volume is proportional to A, and the mass is proportional to A as well. Density = mass/volume is therefore independent of A, so it is unchanged. Check with the two values: A = 27 gives r = 3r0 and V = 27(4/3)pi r0^3; A = 216 gives r = 6r0 and V = 216(4/3)pi r0^3, the same volume per nucleon

S03-13.method: find the new edge length, then compare total areas
S03-13.working: 1000 cubes means 10 along each edge, so each side is 1.0/10 = 0.10 cm. Original area 6 x 1.0^2 = 6.0 cm^2. Each small cube 6 x 0.10^2 = 0.060 cm^2, so the total is 1000 x 0.060 = 60 cm^2. Ratio 60/6.0 = 10. Check by the rule: cutting into n pieces along each edge multiplies the total area by n, and n = 10

S03-14.method: separate the variables, then integrate the speed
S03-14.working: a = dv/dt = -kv separates to dv/v = -k dt, so v = u e^(-kt). Distance = integral of v dt from 0 to infinity = u/k. Check by dimensions: [u/k] = (m s^-1)/(s^-1) = m, a length. Check the size: a larger k stops the particle sooner, and u/k falls as k rises

S03-15.method: impulse is the area under the force-time graph
S03-15.working: the graph is a triangle of base 0.20 s and height 20 N, so impulse = (1/2) x 0.20 x 20 = 2.0 N s. That is the change in momentum from rest, so v = 2.0/2.0 = 1.0 m/s. Check the size: an average force of 10 N acting for 0.20 s on 2.0 kg gives 10 x 0.20/2.0 = 1.0 m/s

S03-16.method: divide the resolved equations to remove N and m
S03-16.working: resolve: N cos(theta) = mg vertically and N sin(theta) = mv^2/r horizontally. Dividing gives tan(theta) = v^2/(rg) = 15^2/(30 x 10) = 225/300 = 0.75, and tan(37 deg) is about 0.75, so theta is 37 deg. Check the direction: a faster car needs a steeper bank, and 0.75 is just below 1, so the angle is just below 45 deg

S03-17.method: stress gives an area, then the circle relation gives the diameter
S03-17.working: W = 1000 x 10 = 1.0e4 N. At the breaking stress A = W/stress = 1.0e4/1.0e9 = 1.0e-5 m^2. For a circle A = pi d^2/4, so d = sqrt(4A/pi) = sqrt(1.273e-5) = 3.57e-3 m, about 3.6 mm. Check the order: a few millimetres is right for a steel cable lifting a tonne, and 36 mm would be a structural column

S03-18.working: d = 1 mm/300 = 3.33e-6 m. The highest order is set by sin(theta) <= 1, so n <= d/lambda = 3.33e-6/5.0e-7 = 6.67 and the largest whole number is 6. Check the next one: n = 7 would need sin(theta) = 7 x 5.0e-7/3.33e-6 = 1.05, which does not exist

S03-19.method: the lens equation, then a separate ratio
S03-19.working: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/20 - 1/30 = (3 - 2)/60 = 1/60, so v = 60 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 60/30 = 2. Check the region: the object sits between f and 2f, which gives a real image beyond 2f magnified by more than one, and 2 is more than one

S03-20.method: convert the ratings to resistances, then share a common current
S03-20.working: R = V^2/P, so R_60 = 240^2/60 = 960 ohm and R_100 = 240^2/100 = 576 ohm. In series the current is common, so each lamp takes I^2 R and the larger resistance takes the larger share; 960 is greater than 576, so the 60 W lamp is brighter. Check numerically: 960:576 = 5:3, total 1536 ohm, I = 240/1536 = 0.156 A, giving 23 W in the 60 W lamp and 14 W in the 100 W lamp

S03-21.method: series capacitors share the voltage inversely with C
S03-21.working: series capacitors carry the same charge, so V = Q/C makes the voltages inversely proportional to the capacitances: 2.0 and 6.0 uF share 12 V in the ratio 6:2 = 3:1, so the 2.0 uF takes 9.0 V. Check: C_series = (2.0 x 6.0)/8.0 = 1.5 uF, Q = 1.5e-6 x 12 = 1.8e-5 C, and V = Q/C = 1.8e-5/2.0e-6 = 9.0 V

S03-22.working: delta_L = L0 alpha delta_T = 2.0 x 1.9e-5 x (120 - 20) = 2.0 x 1.9e-5 x 100 = 3.8e-3 m = 3.8 mm. Check the size: the fractional change is 1.9e-5 x 100 = 1.9e-3, about two parts in a thousand, and 1.9e-3 x 2.0 m = 3.8 mm

S03-23.method: multiply the mass defect by c squared
S03-23.working: E = delta_m c^2 = 3.6e-30 x (3.0e8)^2 = 3.6e-30 x 9.0e16 = 3.24e-13 J. Check the order: 1e-30 kg is about 0.6 atomic mass units converted wholly, which should be a few hundred keV to a couple of MeV, and 3.24e-13 J is about 2.0 MeV

S03-24.method: photon energy minus the work function, read as volts
S03-24.working: photon energy = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. Maximum kinetic energy = 3.1 - 2.0 = 1.1 eV, and the stopping potential in volts is numerically the maximum kinetic energy in electronvolts, so 1.1 V. Check the direction: the stopping potential must be less than the photon energy, and it is the difference rather than the sum

S03-25.working: weight = 0.50 x 10 = 5.0 N. Upthrust = rho V g = 1000 x 2.0e-4 x 10 = 2.0 N. Reading = 5.0 - 2.0 = 3.0 N. Check the density: the stone is 0.50/2.0e-4 = 2500 kg/m^3, denser than water, so it sinks and the reading stays positive
